slots.hypothesis: The core is the only part of the snapshot heads whose removal makes them collapse: knocking it out drops head 2 from 0.79 to -0.55 and head 1 from 0.91 to -1.99, and it appears in 48 of 114 candidates (+0.75, p 0.0005). It measures the variance of the log market-cap level, which is mostly daily-frequency, overnight and inter-day variance that the intraday-volatility control cannot see. The snapshot only ever used it inside cross_regbeta(day_quantile_q75(Volume), .). The new periphery leaves out cross_regbeta, q75, LimitWidth, cs_median and day_pos_ratio. It has four parts: (1) variance ratio and decomposition (Lo-MacKinlay; Yang-Zhang), as log core minus log intraday variance, log core minus log open-to-close variance, and a per-stock 120-day time-series residual; (2) slowing the core (120-day mean, median, upper tail), because a single 20-point level variance has a CV of about 0.9 and on its own scores -2.71, which is mostly turnover cost; (3) change relative to its own history (zscore, log ratio, vol-of-vol); (4) comparison within peers using size and board buckets, an Amihud-style variance per unit of turnover, and a scale-free volume-volatility cross_corr (mixture-of-distributions hypothesis). Why it should hold out of sample: the A-share low-volatility premium is behavioral and insensitive to the estimation window (Blitz 2021), and every seed works on a 60-120 day scale, so turnover stays low. 14 seeds.

How unstable a stock's trading activity is from day to day (volume-of-volume), and how unstable its risk is (vol-of-vol), are overpriced, so the stable end should earn more. Chordia, Subrahmanyam & Anshuman (2001) found that a higher CV of turnover means lower returns. The proposed mechanism is attention shocks driving retail overpricing (Barber-Odean 2008), with Baltussen et al. (2018) for vol-of-vol. The seeds are scale-free cross-day variability measures: CV of daily amount over 60/120 days, std of log amount, log turnover and log q75 minute amount, log peak/median and log upper-tail/lower-tail ratios, std of daily log changes, mean |cross_zscore| of amount, CV of 5-day intraday volatility, std of log intraday volatility, a size-bucket z-score and a rank blend. The idea comes from this batch: every head's outer cross_regbeta(day_quantile_q75(Volume), Y) = corr*sd(Y)/sd(X) is ranked mainly by 1/sd(X), and swapping Volume for Amt helped. In the heads, though, dispersion is mixed up with the volume level. All five controls are level measures, while these seeds are scale-free variability measures. The direction is picked on train; the competing Gervais-Kaniel-Mingelgrin high-volume premium would flip it. 14 seeds.

I wrote the round-1 plan for seed 807, added a round-1 section to the seed notebook, and ran the c06_check plan check: it reported ADMISSIBLE with exit code 0. The plan has not been audited yet, and I did not run anything on the server.

**Slot a, E (deep dig):** the fixed core is `ts_var(LogFloatCap, 20)`, item 7 on the core card. It is the only part of the snapshot heads whose removal makes them collapse. I chose it over the analysis's preferred core A because core A carries a dead `add(cs_median(day_pos_ratio(Open)), .)` term, and the bare core leaves the GP more room to grow outside it. None of the 14 seeds uses `cross_regbeta`, `day_quantile_q75`, `LimitWidth`, `cs_median` or `day_pos_ratio`. They wrap the core four ways:
- variance ratio (core relative to intraday variance), the Yang-Zhang overnight split, and a per-stock regression residual;
- slow 60-120 day statistics of the core, since turnover cost decides most scores here;
- the core relative to its own history, including vol-of-vol;
- comparison within size or board buckets, variance per unit of turnover, and a volume-volatility `cross_corr`.

**Slot b, N (new idea):** stocks whose trading activity, or whose volatility, is unstable from day to day are overpriced. This draws on Chordia, Subrahmanyam & Anshuman 2001, Barber-Odean 2008 and Baltussen et al. 2018. The batch hint is that every head's outer regression is ranked mainly by the inverse spread of volume. The 14 seeds turn that into scale-free measures of variation across days; all five controls are level measures.

**R (12 variants):**
- Head 3 gets six: switch Volume to Amt and lengthen the window to 60, free the `ts_var(LogFloatCap, 50)` term that `cs_median` currently wastes, `cross_corr` and t-value versions to test whether the outer score is scale or co-movement, and a size bucket.
- Head 2 gets six: window 60, BoardCode or LogFloatCap buckets, LogTotalCap instead of LogFloatCap, `ts_var` window 40, and a `cross_corr` version. It keeps Volume so the two replacements don't end up as the same formula.

All ratios are written as log differences, which avoids blow-ups from dividing by near-zero values. The seeds avoid `cross_rank` and unsmoothed `cs_bucket_rank`, because they would fail the distinct-value gate.

**Notebook:** two corrections to the analysis are recorded. The 3 heads are really only 2 independent ideas. The analysis's N1 idea (dividing by a cross-sectional median) is an exact no-op once values are ranked each day.

Predictions:
- Slot a produces 1-3 heads, most likely the slowed versions, direction -1; about 60% chance of at least one head at 0.5 or above.
- Slot b produces 0-2 heads from the CV of daily amount, direction -1; about 40%.
- Head 3 is replaced by an Amt variant scoring 1.0 or more (80%).
- The `cross_corr` variants score at least 0.3 below the `cross_regbeta` ones (60%).

**Main risk:** the slowed seeds in slot a may correlate with the volatility control at about 0.7-0.8, so the correlation table could strike 1-3 of them. That would still leave enough seeds for the slot to pass.
